newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Capel buys four mln Fairfax shares-brokers.
newsitem.headline: Capel buys four mln Fairfax shares-brokers.

text.p: Shares in newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd topped the Australian share market's turnover list on Tuesday with HSBC James Capel buying more than four million shares, brokers said.
The head of one institutional dealing desk said more than three million of the shares were bought from Merrill Lynch.
The broker said he believed Capel was seeking more Fairfax shares as Capel had not on-sold any of the stock.
He said Brierley Investments Ltd of New Zealand was the "obvious bet" as the most likely client of Capel's but this could not be confirmed.

Brierley Investments is the largest shareholder in Fairfax with a 20 percent stake. As a foreign company it can only increase its stake by launching a full takeover bid or by using the "creep" provisions of local companies law which allows firms to buy three percent of the stock every six months.
For Brierley, the waitingperiod ended on Monday as it acquired its holding from Canada's Conrad Black on December 16.
It has said it wanted to acquire up to 50 percent of the publisher, the oldest in Australia, and a mooted target for Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd, which has a 15 percent stake.
Merrill Lynch acquired 22.75 million Fairfax shares, representing 2.99 percent, from a trading account operated by Westpac Banking Corp on June 6.
At the time, brokers speculated that this stake would be on-sold to Brierley in a few weeks when the "creep provision" took effect.
Fairfax shares were one cent firmer at A$3.28 at 11.40 a.m. (0110 GMT). Turnover had increased to 5.52 million shares.
The company has 758.76 million shares on issue and a market capitalisation of A$2.48 billion based on its latest price.
